title: Readable objects: ledgers, letters, environment reveals
next_step: hand to a critic. NOT DONE and not faked: 63 demanded reveals still have no route. 24 ledgers/letters are still unwritten and `reveal-route-audit` section A.2 names every one; 18 environment sources want an ARRIVAL reader against a place register, which is a different piece and is ruled on per-source in reports/runs/W1-READABLES/environment-source-ruling.json. `viability-walk` still reports 0/40 and still stops at Q-MAIN-06 — see `THE WALK DID NOT MOVE` below; that is its allow-list, not the world, and the fix belongs to the walk's owner.
notes: THE FINDING. `deceit.revealed_by[].channel` splits nine ways and W1-18 r2 routed the two whose sources are PEOPLE. Of the 73 left, 52 were `ledger` (28 demanded), `letter` (6) and `environment` (18), and they were blocked on CONTENT: 33 of 34 ledger sources and all 10 letter sources named an `item_*` id that was not an object anywhere in `game/data/`. The last round was right not to wire a reader to them. This round wrote the objects.

A LEDGER IS A BOOK WITH A DIFFERENT NOUN, and the answer to the brief's question is yes — use the book path, and I did. `Engine._bookKnowledgeIndex()` already matches a `revealed_by` row's `source` against a book's `knowledge_key` and unions the reveal id into `ctx.knowledge` for everything in `sim.quest.booksRead`. The whole engine change for the channel is one constant: `DOCUMENT_CHANNELS = {book, ledger, letter}` in `sim/quest/reveal-routes.js`, and `_bookKnowledgeIndex`'s `rev.channel !== 'book'` becomes a membership test. No second mechanism, no second index, no second reader. `game/data/books/**` already ships a book of `kind: "ledger"` (the Tally's fourth volume), which is the corpus saying the same thing before I got here.

WHAT THE NOUN DOES CHANGE IS THE VERB, and that is the one piece of new world code. A prop may carry `readable_book`; `Engine._takePropPending()` then OPENS it where it stands through `UISystem.open('book')` — the player's own door, the one W1-LIBRARY found — instead of pocketing it, and the prop is `takeable: false`. This is not tidiness. Q-MAIN-06 ships a failure state `fail_took_the_books` whose cause is *"the player removes a volume of the Tally from the archive"*, and Hosk-Vei's own directions say he will not let the books leave the room. An archive whose only interaction was `take` would have made that failure the single thing a player could do in it. The interact PROMPT follows the object too: `read`, not `take`.

PLACEMENT, and it is half the work. The interior record's `readable` was one `{id, title}` pair drawn as a book-shaped box on a shelf — 83 of 115 rooms have one and NOT ONE OF THEM HAD ANYTHING WRITTEN IN IT. It may now be a LIST and a member may name a `book`. `render/interior.js` places each on its own wall slot and publishes `placements.readables`; `Engine._furnishInterior()` spawns a prop per document. A record with no `book` is the shelf dressing it always was and draws exactly as before.

THE PLACEMENT RULE, so a critic can check it rather than take it: a document lives in the room where the person who owns it stands, and those posts are not invented here — they are `npc.post.at_building`, authored by W1-GIVER-PRESENCE, and `travelToGiver()` is the world's own call that walks you to them. `tools/readables/place-documents.mjs` is the whole table with a comment per room. TWO EXCEPTIONS, DECLARED: Q-MAIN-07's yard book is at `blackrose-shrine` because this build has no interior for the cutting yard behind the reed-walk, and Q-DEEP-01's `the-sap-and-the-knife` is at `helstrom-undertemple` because Speaker Teel-Ashaan has no `post` in `game/data/npcs/**` at all. Both are in the file as judgements rather than lookups.

WHAT WAS WRITTEN. 9 documents, 5,075 words, all T4 (RI-LOR03's diary/letters/ledgers taxon, target 700 w). `game/data/books/the-books-in-evidence.json` — the grandmother's yard book at Blackrose (698 w), Cuiro-Vaneth's private manifest at Archon (556), the Wet Ledger's book behind the counter (563), the Gideon compact's share book (482), the rootkeepers' list of the seven who opened a well (536), and the Steward's letter in Jel taken off a body (430). `game/data/books/the-drowned-tally.json` gains the TENTH volume (the leaves either side of the thirty-ninth year, where the return column stops being level, with the archive's own note on the licence roll at the back), the APPENDIX (what was measured of previous readers after the tasting — the term Hosk-Vei omits), and the SEVERANCES (three in four hundred years).

ONE OF Q-MAIN-06'S TWO REVEALS NEEDED NO PROSE AT ALL. `item_tally_volume_four` -> `the-drowned-tally-fourth-volume`, which W1-LIBRARY wrote and which ends *"I. M., Steward of the Count"*. The quest has been naming it since it was authored and the only thing missing was the `knowledge_key` that links the two. One field.

PROVED IN THE RUNNING GAME, `tools/quests/document-route-world.mjs`, report at reports/runs/W1-READABLES/document-route-world.json. 6 legs run, 6 passed. THE ONLY ACT IS `interact`, PRESSED THROUGH THE INPUT PIPELINE — there is no read verb in the harness and this tool does not add one; it queues the button and steps the fixed loop. Q-MAIN-06: walk into soulrest-court-steps, stand 1 m from the shelf, press it, the book screen comes up on `the-drowned-tally-tenth-volume`, `booksRead` gains it, and `questResolutions('Q-MAIN-06')` refusals naming `rev_the_curve_predates` go 2 -> 0. Also Q-MAIN-06/rev_the_steward_named 1 -> 0, Q-MAIN-07 2 -> 0, Q-MAIN-08 3 -> 0, Q-MAIN-10 2 -> 0, Q-MAIN-30 2 -> 0.

PROHIBITED IN THAT RUN and asserted against the tool's own bytes: `openMenu` (the harness door into the book screen — calling it would skip the object, the room and the reach, which are the three things being measured), `questReveal`, `questSetFlag`, `__ENGINE`. DECLARED GRANTS: `questOpen`/`learnTopic` (only the `opens_by` topics the refusal itself names — the offer gate is `mainline-findability.mjs`'s question), `travelToGiver`/`enterInterior`, `teleport` (crossing the room; getting a body from the doorway to the shelf is the movement system's question and its failure would be reported here as a failure of reading), and `questResolve` ON PREREQUISITE QUESTS ONLY, taking only a resolution the gate itself reports available and preferring the non-violent one — the same two verbs `viability-walk` allows itself.

CONTROLS, both of which bit. (1) OUT OF REACH: stand in the same room at the point on the room's own floor whose nearest document is furthest away, press the same button — nothing opens, nothing is read, on all 6 legs. The first version of this control placed the body by eye and it LANDED INSIDE THE REACH OF A DIFFERENT DOCUMENT and read it, which is the control working one step before it was written down. (2) THE WRONG DOCUMENT: read a different book off the same shelf; the refusal does not move, on all 6. Where a room holds only one document the control comes free from the chain, which had to read other documents to get there and did not move this refusal either. (3) A leg FAILS if the document was already read or the reveal already known before the act.

DELETE-THE-FIX 1 (the channel), on a COPY of the tree at `--entry <copy>/game/index.html` so nothing on the shared tree was perturbed (RULES.md rule 17): put `_bookKnowledgeIndex`'s test back to `rev.channel !== 'book'` and Q-MAIN-06 goes 2/2 -> 0/2. The book still OPENS and `booksRead` still goes 0 -> 2 — the reading happens and the knowledge does not arrive, which is exactly the seam under test and not some other change wearing its name.

DELETE-THE-FIX 2 (the verb): disable the `readable_book` branch in `_takePropPending` on a second copy and the same two legs go 0/2 with `screen world, book null` and `booksRead 0 -> 0`. The two arms genuinely differ from each other as well as from the fix: arm 1 reads and learns nothing, arm 2 does not read.

DELETE-THE-FIX 3 (the placement half of the audit): `reveal-route-audit --falsify unplace` forgets all 28 book placements and section A goes 58 -> 43, `ledger` 9 -> 0, `letter` 1 -> 0 and `book` 5 -> 0. That last number is the point — see the next note.

FOUND WHILE PROVING MINE, AND IT IS SOMEBODY ELSE'S HEADLINE: NONE of the nine `knowledge_key` books W1-LIBRARY shipped was an object in any room. The audit had been scoring the five `channel: book` rows green since that round on the strength of the BOOK EXISTING, so those five reveals were reachable only through `openMenu('book')`, which is the harness door. `documentRoute()` now requires BOTH halves — the document exists AND a room or an item names it — and all nine are placed. This makes the audit stricter than the number it inherited; the delete-the-fix above is what proves the second half is load-bearing rather than a definition I moved.

A REAL WORLD DEFECT THE BROWSER FOUND AND THE DATA COULD NOT. `sim/settlement.js` takes `interact` for the way OUT within `DOOR_REACH_M` = 2.6 m of `continuity.interior_spawn`, and it runs BEFORE the engine's prop reach — so a document drawn on the shelf beside the doorway can never be read: press the button at it and you walk out of the room. `the-archon-true-manifest` landed exactly there and the tool refused to run the leg and named the distance rather than reporting it as a reading failure. Fixed in `render/interior.js` by excluding wall slots within 3.8 m of the interior spawn from the READABLE slot pool (the door's 2.6 m plus the prop's 1 m stand-off plus a margin). This moves where the shelf book is drawn in some of the 83 rooms that already had one; they are decorative props and no check pins their position.

SECOND WORLD FINDING, reported not fixed: `interact` is one button with several claimants and a CONVERSATION swallows every later press. A press at the empty spot in the Court's archive greeted the archivist standing in it and every subsequent press went to the conversation — which is why my first three runs read `screen world` at a shelf a metre away. The tool now closes a conversation it opened by accident and records it under `presses_that_reached_a_person_instead`. Whether a player should be able to press interact twice and have the second press mean something is a UI question and is not mine.

THE WALK DID NOT MOVE, and this is the honest answer to the brief's question. `viability-walk.mjs` still reports 0/40, still `quests completed per signature 5..5`, and all 40 still stop at Q-MAIN-06 with the byte-identical message. THE REASON IS ITS ALLOW-LIST, NOT THE WORLD: `ALLOWED_VERBS` is creation, observation, `travelToGiver`, `questOpen`, `questResolve` and the four conversation verbs. There is no `enterInterior`, no `listEntities`, no `queueInputs`/`stepFrames`, no `teleport` — the walk cannot walk into a room and open a book, so the document channel is invisible to it exactly as the `book` channel has been since W1-LIBRARY. I did NOT widen somebody else's grant fence; that is the whole point of the fence and the change belongs to its owner.

WHAT WOULD MOVE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. `document-route-world.mjs --chain` plays the main line twice with the same two verbs the walk allows itself, differing only in whether opening a document is permitted. READING ALLOWED: 10 of 32 mainline quests finished, stopping at Q-MAIN-11 on `res_walk_it: you do not know rev_the_rhythm`. READING REFUSED: 5 of 32, stopping at Q-MAIN-06 on `res_the_number: you do not know rev_the_curve_predates` — the walk's own stop, reproduced. So the wall moved five quests down the chain, from a ledger that did not exist to a place that has no arrival reader. Report at reports/runs/W1-READABLES/document-route-chain.json.

THE ENVIRONMENT RULING, one decision per source, at reports/runs/W1-READABLES/environment-source-ruling.json. FIRST, A CORRECTION TO THE COUNT I WAS HANDED: FOUR of the 27 environment sources are sentences rather than ids, not nine — `the cough on the lichen beds`, `the chalk on eleven doors`, `the stopper mark, matching the ones at the cut sapwell`, `the cut itself, on the shaded side`. Two of the four are demanded. VERDICTS: 18 PLACE (11 `loc_*`/`environment_*` ids, the 4 Ash Gallery `posts` — where a `post` is a keeper's STATION and the `item_` prefix is misleading — and 3 of the 4 sentences). They want an ARRIVAL reader calling `learnFrom('place', id)` against a place register, and the world already has the shape of it in `world/opacity.js`'s `met()` route model and `pois.json`. 5 DOCUMENT (`item_distraint_order_wax`, `item_prefect_returns_press`, `item_tally_sheet_fold`, `item_chapter_room_recension`, `letter_held_to_the_lamp`): papers whose tell happens to be physical, and prose carries wax and a crease and a mismatched ink as well as it carries a number — amend `channel` to `ledger`/`letter`, write the document, place it, and this round's machinery takes them with no new code. 4 ITEM (`item_lead_ring_seal`, `item_salt_sack_wire`, `item_stale_mortuary_seal`, and the stopper-mark sentence): objects with no words on them; they want an item-examined reader beside `takeProp`, and writing a page for a lead disc would be inventing a document nobody wrote.

A DATA DEFECT WORTH SOMEBODY'S TIME: Q-XULA-05's `rev_court_ledger` declares `channel: ledger` with `source: ledgerer-hosk-vei`, which is a PERSON id. Either the channel is wrong (it is a `talk_to_target`) or the source is. Reported by `check-quests` and by the audit; not amended by me, because guessing which half is wrong is the quest author's call.

NEW CONTENT CHECK, armed only after the data existed (rule 13). `tools/check-quests.mjs` now warns loudly, by name, on (a) a document channel whose `source` has no document written for it — 24 rows on this tree — and (b) a document that exists and is an object in no room — 0 rows. WARNING, EXIT 0, deliberately, for the same reason as its attribute-scale neighbour: 24 of the 39 demanded document rows are content nobody has written yet and a fail-closed assertion would take the check red for every agent on the box. PROVED IT GOES RED: on a copy of the tree with the tenth volume's placement removed, arm (b) fires and names `Q-MAIN-06.rev_the_curve_predates ... written, in no room`. `--self-test` is 10/10 unchanged.

PROSE. `node tools/check-prose.mjs --verbose`: `game/data/books/the-books-in-evidence.json` is `ok` on every gated metric (3,265 w). `the-drowned-tally.json` was RED on four metrics before this round (questions, exclamations, sting, contractions) and is now green on all four — my 1,810 words pulled the file over its floors and took the sting rate 4.92 -> under the 3.98 ceiling. Its one remaining warning is `"that is what/why/all" x2`, which is in `the-seventh-recension`'s prose and not mine; I left it rather than edit another piece's bytes, the same discipline W1-LIBRARY r2 recorded. Whole-run exit 0.

GATES at b900460: boot-check PASS, check-data PASS (557 indexed files), check-content PASS (383 resolutions, none lost), check-quests PASS + self-test 10/10, check-prose exit 0, corpus-index exit 0, publish PASS (42 verdicts, all plotted, image resolves). `reveal-route-audit` still exits 1 by design — it goes green only when EVERY demanded reveal has a route and 63 do not. It is not in INDEX.md's gate table and breaks no gate.

NO NEW SAVE FIELDS. Reading a document writes `sim.quest.booksRead`, which `game/src/save/state.js` has carried as `dialogue.books_read` since W1-LIBRARY r2 and which `game/data/save-manifest.json` already declares durable and id-sorted. Nothing new to round-trip, so rule 7 has nothing new to catch here.

THE TREE MOVED UNDER ME. `game/data/books/the-books-in-evidence.json` and my edits to `the-drowned-tally.json` were banked by a neighbour's commit while I worked (they are in `git ls-files` and show no diff); I ran no commit. Every number above was re-taken at b900460 afterwards. I regenerated `docs/shots/2026-08-07-w1-19-r3-the-reveals-no-play-produces.png` by accident while adding the `--round w1-readables` arm to the chart tool and RESTORED it from HEAD, md5-verified; W1-19-r3's picture is byte-identical to what it published. The chart gained a FLAG rather than a second file, which is that tool's own stated doctrine.

LOAD, per rule 26, and it is worse than I would like. The box sat at 18 concurrent `headless_shell` and a load average of 13.9-16.2 for the first half of the run and had climbed to 53 browsers and a load average of 36.1 by the final re-run at b900460. That is far over rule 21's ~8 ceiling; I waited for it to drop, it did not, and I then ran ONE browser at a time and kept it for each run, exactly as W1-18 r2 did under the same conditions. NO TIMING FIGURE IS QUOTED ANYWHERE in this piece — every number is a count or a boolean and neither moves with load — and the browser count and load average at each run are stamped into reports/runs/W1-READABLES/document-route-world.json alongside the commit.

OWNERSHIP. `redundant_with` names W1-18-r2 and W1-19-r3 because this is the continuation of their finding on the same files (`reveal-routes.js`, `reveal-route-audit.mjs`, the chart), both `done` with no live claims; W1-LIBRARY-r2 because I extended its reader and placed its books; W1-04-r2 because we both touch `game/src/engine.js` and `game/src/render/interior.js` — my interior change is additive (a list where there was a scalar, and a slot filter) and touches neither settlement population nor the props/lights/containers path that piece is measuring. Everything else is `docs/shots/` and `reports/blog-feed.jsonl`, which rule 27 requires every piece to touch.

NOT DONE, PLAINLY. 63 of 121 demanded reveals still have no route: 24 ledgers and letters with no document written (named one by one in audit section A.2 and by check-quests), 18 environment sources needing an arrival reader, 9 eavesdrop rows needing a proximity-and-not-noticed reader against `sim/stealth` (W1-18 r2's reasoning still stands), 1 corpse row, and 10 person-channel rows whose source is not in `game/data/npcs/**`. Q-MAIN-11 and Q-MAIN-15 are the two quests with every resolution still blocked, and both are blocked on `environment`. The main line now walks to Q-MAIN-11 and stops there.

DECLARED OVERLAPS, per rule 16. Every piece `ownership.mjs --conflicts` pairs me with is in `redundant_with`. The overlap with W1-03, W1-06*, W1-12, W1-13-r3 and critic-w1-04-r2 is `game/src/engine.js` and `game/src/render/renderer.js`, which most of this wave touches; my edits there are four additive blocks (one import, one channel-set membership test, the `readable_book` branch of `_takePropPending`, the readables loop in `_furnishInterior`) plus one cache-key line in the renderer that had to change because `readable` became a list. The rest is `reports/blog-feed.jsonl` and `docs/shots/`, which rule 27 requires every piece to touch.

EVERY NUMBER IN THIS FILE IS AT b900460, per rule 12. The browser proof was re-run at that commit after a neighbour banked the tree under me, so the report artifact and the static audit agree about which code they are a claim about: reports/runs/W1-READABLES/document-route-world.json stamps commit b900460, 6 legs run, 6 passed.
headline: A LEDGER IS A BOOK WITH A DIFFERENT NOUN AND A DIFFERENT VERB. 34 `ledger` and 10 `letter` rows named a document as the source of a truth a resolution demands and not one was an object in this build; the last round correctly refused to wire a reader to them. Nine documents written (5,075 words), 21 placed on shelves in 8 rooms, and the existing book reader routes them unchanged. Demanded reveals with a route in play 48 -> 58 of 121; quests with EVERY resolution blocked 7 -> 2. Q-MAIN-06 is proved dead-to-alive in a browser: walk into the archive, press interact at the shelf, and the refusal all 40 walked signatures stop on goes 2 -> 0.

baseline.viability_walk: 0/40, all 40 stop at Q-MAIN-06 on rev_the_curve_predates
